fieldValues.title: When retiring a section/subsection record by edge-count, split the unit at roughly 10-15 contains children -- larger records risk a silently dropped precedes/contains edge in one session
fieldValues.summary: srs#710's dispatch offered 10 section records to retire in one unit. Five with 0-6 contains children each retyped cleanly (create successor concept, derived-from new->old, move every contains/precedes edge, resync Part membership, add the two allowlist/exclusion entries) with each step validated individually. The remaining two, Extensions (35 contains children) and Foundation Group (Core) (19 children), were deferred rather than attempted in the same session: moving that many edges by hand-driven CLI relation-create calls, one at a time, with no bulk-move verb, is exactly the shape of task where one edge gets missed and the corresponding check either doesn't fire (because the check is instance-scoped, not corpus-scoped) or fires days later on an unrelated PR.
fieldValues.rationale: No CLI verb exists yet for 'move all contains/precedes edges from record A to record B' (srs#178's identity-preserving retype would remove the need entirely) -- until it does, this pattern applies to any future unit retiring a section/subsection record: measure contains-child count first (srs record list / relation list, not the issue body's possibly-stale number), and split the batch so no single session moves edges for a record with more than roughly 10-15 children. Would go stale the moment a bulk relation-retarget or identity-preserving retype verb ships (srs#178 or an equivalent), at which point edge-count stops being the risk driver and this carried_context should be superseded rather than silently ignored.
